newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 5.00 cents higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 5.00 cents higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 5.00 cents higher Thursday as traders expect the market to bounce back after Wednesday's weak finish.
Some New York traders also said London's inability to reach its down $100 pre-opening call contributed to the CSCE higher call.
London robusta futures slumped early Thursday, but roaster price-fixing absorbed losses. LIFFE September was down $15 at the midday break at $2,100 a tonne, after bottoming at $2,060.

Wednesday, New York arabica futures fell sharply in the nearby contracts, as news Colombia opened "unlimited" coffee registrations weighed on the market. July tumbled 12.65 cents per lb, to 251.55 cents, after ranging between 264.50 and 250.00 cents. September fell 7.95 cents to 225.10 cents, while the back months closed 6.15 lower to 2.50 higher.
The July/September spread, a barometer of nearby availability, shrank to 26.45 cents from 31.15 cents at the close on Tuesday.
Technically, traders said July would find resistance at 259.00-260.00, then 263.00. Support was seen at Monday's low of 247.50, followed by 235.00.
After Wednesday's close, the CSCE said certified coffee stocks fell by 283 60-kg bags as of June 3, to 45,702 bags, There were 1,320 bags pending grading, the exchange said.

Weather Services Corp said Thursday no damaging cold weather was expected to hit Brazil's coffee belt this weekend, although temperatures will drop to below normal levels. The situation continues to bear close watching, it said.
